concepts.description: The aggregate of people living together in a more or less ordered community.
The activities associated with the governance of a country or area.
A nation or territory considered as an organized political community under one government.
A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state.
A state in which supreme power is held by the people and their elected representatives.
A government by a dictator with absolute power.
A form of government with a monarch at the head.
A body of fundamental principles according to which a state is governed.
The fundamental law of a nation, specifically the German constitution.
A right which is believed to belong justifiably to every person.
A legally recognized subject or national of a state or commonwealth.
All the inhabitants of a particular town, area, or country.
The citizens of a particular nation or ethnic group.
A group of people living in the same place or having a particular characteristic in common.
A single human being as distinct from a group, class, or family.
To conduct the policy, actions, and affairs of a state or organization.
The governing body of a nation, state, or community.
A legislative body of government.
A government department under the direction of a minister.
The head of the government in Germany.
The elected head of a republican state.
A head of a government department.
The elected head of a city, town, or other municipality.
A person who is professionally involved in politics.
A person chosen or appointed to act or speak for others, especially in a legislative assembly.
A person in the public sector employed by a government department or agency.
The process or activity of running an organization or government.
A system of government in which most of the important decisions are made by state officials.
To choose someone to hold public office by voting.
A formal and organized choice by vote of a person for a political office or other position.
A person who votes or has the right to vote at an election.
A person who applies for a job or is nominated for election.
A formal expression of opinion or choice in an election.
The greater number, especially more than half of the total number.
The smaller number or part, especially a number that is less than half the whole number.
The political party or group that is not in government and opposes its policies.
An alliance for combined action, especially a temporary alliance of political parties forming a government.
An organized group of people who have the same political aims and beliefs.
An organized course of action to achieve a goal, especially in politics.
The process of voting in an election or a survey of public opinion.
A system of ideas and ideals, especially one which forms the basis of economic or political theory.
A set of political goals or principles of a party.
The improvement or amendment of what is wrong, corrupt, or unsatisfactory.
To make changes in order to improve something.
To express an objection to what someone has said or done.
A statement or action expressing disapproval of or objection to something.
A public meeting or march protesting against something or expressing views.
A forcible overthrow of a government or social order, in favor of a new system.
To take part in a public meeting or march to express political views.
The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants.
The state of being equal, especially in status, rights, and opportunities.
Unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals with a common interest.
The ability or willingness to tolerate something, in particular the existence of opinions or behavior that one does not necessarily agree with.
Just behavior or treatment.
Lack of fairness or justice.
The system of rules which a particular country or community recognizes as regulating the actions of its members.
An entitlement to have or obtain something or to act in a certain way.
A moral or legal obligation.
A separate clause or paragraph of a legal document or constitution.
A distinct section of a piece of writing, specifically in a legal text.
A body of people presided over by a judge, judges, or a magistrate, and acting as a tribunal in civil and criminal cases.
A public official appointed to decide cases in a court of law.
A person who practices or studies law; an attorney.
The civil force of a national or local government, responsible for the prevention and detection of crime and the maintenance of public order.
A person holding a position of authority in a police force.
An action or omission that constitutes an offense and is punishable by law.
A person who has committed a crime.
A person who carries out a harmful, illegal, or immoral act.
A person harmed, injured, or killed as a result of a crime, accident, or other event or action.
A person who sees an event, typically a crime or accident, take place.
The available body of facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true or valid.
The action of seizing someone and taking them into custody.
To seize someone by legal authority and take them into custody.
A building in which people are legally held as a punishment for a crime they have committed or while awaiting trial.
The infliction or imposition of a penalty as retribution for an offense.
To inflict a penalty on someone as retribution for an offense, fault, or a mistake.
A sum of money exacted as a penalty by a court of law or other authority.
A formal examination of evidence before a judge, and typically before a jury, in order to decide guilt in a case of criminal or civil proceedings.
A decision on a disputed issue in a civil or criminal case.
Freedom from disturbance; tranquility.
A state of armed conflict between different nations or states or different groups within a nation or state.
A serious disagreement or argument, typically a protracted one.
A time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger.
A line separating two political or geographical areas, especially countries.
An official document issued by a government, certifying the holder's identity and citizenship and entitling them to travel under its protection to and from foreign countries.
An endorsement on a passport indicating that the holder is allowed to enter, leave, or stay for a specified period of time in a country.
Movement of people to a new area or country in order to find work or better living conditions.
To move from one area or country to settle in another.
The action of coming to live permanently in a foreign country.
A person who has been forced to leave their country in order to escape war, persecution, or natural disaster.
The protection granted by a nation to someone who has left their native country as a political refugee.
A person who has left their home country as a political refugee and is seeking asylum in another.
The status of belonging to a particular nation.
The process of integrating a person or group into a larger community.
To mix with and join society or a group of people, often changing to suit their way of life, habits, and customs.
The wealth and resources of a country or region, especially in terms of the production and consumption of goods and services.
An area or arena in which commercial dealings are conducted.
The action of buying and selling goods and services.
A current medium of exchange in the form of coins and banknotes.
A compulsory contribution to state revenue, levied by the government on workers' income and business profits or added to the cost of some goods, services, and transactions.
Tax levied directly on personal income.
A tax on the amount by which the value of an article has been increased at each stage of its production or distribution.
An estimate of income and expenditure for a set period of time, specifically for a state.
Something, typically money, that is owed or due.
A general increase in prices and fall in the purchasing value of money.
The process of increasing in physical size or economic value.
Work, especially hard physical work.
The state of being unemployed.
An organized association of workers, often in a trade or profession, formed to protect and further their rights and interests.
A refusal to work organized by a body of employees as a form of protest.
To refuse to work as a form of protest, typically in an attempt to gain a concession or concessions from an employer.
A fixed regular payment, typically paid on a daily or weekly basis, made by an employer to an employee.
A fixed regular payment, typically paid on a monthly basis but often expressed as an annual sum, made by an employer to an employee.
The lowest wage permitted by law or by a special agreement.
Financial support given to people in need.
A system of providing assistance to people with little or no income.
Insurance that covers the whole or a part of the risk of a person incurring medical expenses.
A regular payment made during a person's retirement from an investment fund to which that person or their employer has contributed during their working life.
The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives or operates.
The physical world and everything in it that is not made by people.
The weather conditions prevailing in an area in general or over a long period.
A change in global or regional climate patterns.
A gradual increase in the overall temperature of the earth's atmosphere generally attributed to the greenhouse effect.
The ability to be maintained at a certain rate or level.
Power derived from the utilization of physical or chemical resources, especially to provide light and heat or to work machines.
The presence in or introduction into the environment of a substance or thing that has harmful or poisonous effects.
The action of protecting someone or something.
To keep safe from harm or injury.
The process of receiving or giving systematic instruction, especially at a school or university.
An institution for educating children.
A high-level educational institution in which students study for degrees and academic research is done.
Facts, information, and skills acquired by a person through experience or education.
The intellectual and practical activity encompassing the systematic study of the structure and behavior of the physical and natural world through observation and experiment.
The systematic investigation into and study of materials and sources in order to establish facts and reach new conclusions.
The main means of mass communication (broadcasting, publishing, and the internet) regarded collectively.
Newspapers and magazines collectively.
The activity or profession of writing for newspapers, magazines, or news websites or preparing news to be broadcast.
Newly received or noteworthy information, especially about recent or important events.
Facts provided or learned about something or someone.
False stories that appear to be news spread on the internet or using other media.
Information, especially of a biased or misleading nature, used to promote or publicize a particular political cause or point of view.
The suppression or prohibition of any parts of books, films, news, etc. that are considered obscene, politically unacceptable, or a threat to security.
The power or right to express one's opinions without censorship, restraint, or legal penalty.
The right of journalists to publish stories without being controlled by the government.
The unjust or prejudicial treatment of different categories of people or things, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.
Prejudice, discrimination, or antagonism directed against someone of a different race based on the belief that one's own race is superior.
Hostility to or prejudice against Jewish people.
Prejudice, stereotyping, or discrimination, typically against women, on the basis of sex.
Dislike of or prejudice against gay people.
The state of being extremely poor.
An abundance of valuable possessions or money.
A person's principles or standards of behavior.
The transmission of customs or beliefs from generation to generation.
Forward or onward movement towards a destination or a better state.
Dishonest or fraudulent conduct by those in power, typically involving bribery.
The capacity or ability to direct or influence the behavior of others or the course of events.
The power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
The state of being free from danger or threat.
A statement of an intention to inflict pain, injury, damage, or other hostile action.
The possibility of suffering harm or injury.
The unlawful use of violence and intimidation, especially against civilians, in the pursuit of political aims.
Moral principles that govern a person's behavior or the conducting of an activity.
Concerned with the principles of right and wrong behavior and the goodness or badness of human character.
The recognition that human beings possess a special value intrinsic to their humanity.
The benefit or interests of all.
Discussion between two or more people or groups, especially one directed towards exploration of a particular subject or resolution of a problem.
A general agreement.
A union or association formed for mutual benefit, especially between countries or organizations.
A formally concluded and ratified agreement between countries.
The profession, activity, or skill of managing international relations.
An official representing a country abroad.
The official residence or offices of an ambassador.
To try to reach an agreement or compromise by discussion with others.
Discussion aimed at reaching an agreement.
An organized military force equipped for fighting on land.
The armed forces of a country.
A person who serves in an army.
The action of defending from or resisting attack.
To resist an attack made on (someone or something); to protect from harm or danger.
Material or logistical assistance provided for humanitarian purposes.
Financial aid given by governments and other agencies to support the economic, environmental, social, and political development of developing countries.
The time or a period of time following the moment of speaking or writing.
A task or situation that tests someone's abilities.
The act or instance of making or becoming different.
The study of past events, particularly in human affairs.
The fact of being who or what a person or thing is.
The arts and other manifestations of human intellectual achievement regarded collectively.
The action of taking part in something.
To take part in an action or endeavor.
The state or quality of being dedicated to a cause, activity, etc.
To participate or become involved in something.
The aggregate of non-governmental organizations and institutions that manifest interests and will of citizens.
A state governed by the rule of law.
The federal principle or system of government.
The process by which businesses or other organizations develop international influence or start operating on an international scale.
The feeling of wanting to know or learn about something or someone.
A group of people seeking to influence politicians or public officials on a particular issue.
The capacity to have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
To have an influence on someone or something.
The state or fact of having a duty to deal with something or of having control over someone.
Having an obligation to do something, or having control over or care for someone, as part of one's job or role.
A means of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
To find an answer to, explanation for, or means of effectively dealing with (a problem or mystery).
A stock or supply of money, materials, staff, and other assets that can be drawn on by a person or organization in order to function effectively.
A new method, idea, product, etc.
A particular attitude towards or way of regarding something; a point of view.
A long and distinct period of history with a particular feature or characteristic.
Relating to the government or the public affairs of a country.
Relating to society or its organization.
Of or concerning the people as a whole.
Belonging to or for the use of one particular person or group of people only.
Relating to an authority or public body and its duties, actions, and responsibilities.
Relating to the law.
Relating to or supporting democracy or its principles.
Willing to respect or accept behavior or opinions different from one's own; open to new ideas.
Holding to traditional attitudes and values and cautious about change or innovation, typically in relation to politics or religion.
Representing or supporting an extreme or progressive section of a political party.
A person who holds extreme or fanatical political or religious views, especially one who resorts to or advocates extreme action.
Free from disturbance; tranquil.
Using or involving physical force intended to hurt, damage, or kill someone or something.
In accordance with the rules or standards; legitimate.
Not based on or behaving according to the principles of equality and justice.
Free from outside control; not depending on another's authority.
Existing, occurring, or carried on between two or more nations.
Relating to or characteristic of a nation; common to a whole nation.
Relating or restricted to a particular area or one's neighborhood.
Relating to the whole world; worldwide.
Having or showing a willingness to act dishonestly in return for money or personal gain.
Relating to the present or recent times as opposed to the remote past.
Existing in or as part of a tradition; long-established.
Happening or developing gradually or in stages; step by step, specifically in political thought.
Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level.
Not connected with religious or spiritual matters.
Relating to or believing in a religion.
Relating to or constituting several cultural or ethnic groups within a society.
Relating to moral principles or the branch of knowledge dealing with these.
To talk about something with another person or group of people.
To argue about a subject, especially in a formal manner.
To have the same opinion about something; concur.
To disagree with and attempt to prevent, especially by argument.
To come to a resolution in the mind as a result of consideration.
To insist on having.
To further the progress of something, especially a cause, venture, or aim; support or encourage.
To give assistance to, especially financially; enable to function or act.
To indicate the faults of someone or something in a disapproving way.
To bring the different elements of a complex activity or organization into a relationship that will ensure efficiency or harmony.
To exercise ultimate power or authority over an area and its people.
A person with the power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
A town or district that has local government.
A political entity characterized by a union of partially self-governing states or regions under a central government.
The authority of a state to govern itself or another state.
A condition or system in which two or more states, groups, principles, sources of authority, etc., coexist.
The refusal to comply with certain laws or to pay taxes and fines, as a peaceful form of political protest.
A situation in which a government is empowered to perform actions or impose policies that it would normally not be permitted to undertake.
To comply with the command, direction, or request of (a person or a law); submit to the authority of.
To break or fail to comply with a rule or formal agreement.
The action of violating someone or something.
A person who gives evidence in a court of law.
To give evidence as a witness in a law court.
A formal account of events given by a witness, defendant, or other party to the police or in a court.
To institute legal proceedings against a person or institution.
To conduct the case for (the party being accused or sued) in a lawsuit.
To charge (someone) with an offense or crime.
A charge or claim that someone has done something illegal or wrong.
Not guilty of a crime or offense.
Culpable of or responsible for a specified wrongdoing.
To release (a person) from the legal consequences of an offense or conviction, and often implicitly from blame.
The action of forgiving or being forgiven for an error or offense.
A group of members of parliament belonging to the same party.
A formal written request, typically one signed by many people, appealing to authority with respect to a particular cause.
A general vote by the electorate on a single political question which has been referred to them for a direct decision.
Laws, considered collectively.
The state of a law or agreement being valid and enforceable.
To sign or give formal consent to (a treaty, contract, or agreement), making it officially valid.
The action of signing or giving formal consent to a treaty, contract, or agreement, making it officially valid.
To exercise a veto against (a decision or proposal).
A constitutional right to reject a decision or proposal made by a law-making body.
A task or action that someone is required to perform as part of their job, especially for the state.
To voluntarily leave a job or other position.
An act of retiring or giving up a position.
The public representative of a country who may also be the head of government.
The period of time for which a parliament is elected.
